title: The Agent Loop Inside Its Sandbox

callouts.label: Repeat or Stop
callouts.hint: Find the left side of the track, where a curved arrow turns back toward the start and a small red octagon with a bar sits beside it.
callouts.description: The model loops back to the first step, or stops. The loop ends when the model judges the task complete, an error stops it, or a limit is reached. Each pass adds the call and its result to the context, so a long loop fills the window fast and an early error compounds.
callouts.tip: Done is a claim, not a fact. Ask for the output of the acceptance check.

callouts.label: Decide
callouts.hint: Find the station at the very top of the track, where the teal worker studies a goal card and a set of tool cards.
callouts.description: The model reads the task, the context, and the tool definitions, then chooses an action. The model never executes anything. It only writes what it wants done. A tool definition is a name, a plain-language description, and the arguments the tool accepts.

callouts.label: Call
callouts.hint: Find the station on the right of the track where the worker holds up a small request slip with a plug-shaped symbol.
callouts.description: The model emits a tool call: a structured request that names a tool and gives specific argument values, such as which file to read. Or it emits a final answer. A call is only a request. Nothing has happened in the world yet.

callouts.label: Subagent Side Loop
callouts.hint: Find the dotted path leaving the track to the upper right, ending at a small second worker inside its own little ring, with a card coming back.
callouts.description: A subagent is a separate agent started by the main agent for one part of a task, with its own context window and often its own restricted tools. It returns a summary. That keeps the main context small, but costs extra tokens, and a lossy summary can hide an error.
callouts.tip: Give parallel agents separate output files, or keep their work read-only.

callouts.label: Rest of Your Machine
callouts.hint: Find the third band of the target on the right, with a closed brick-red padlock and a key shape lying outside the inner rings.
callouts.description: Outside the project sit your home folder, credential files, and other projects. In Chapter 8's illustrative policy, any read or write outside the project and any read of key files is denied. A sandbox enforces this, so even a misbehaving command simply fails.

callouts.label: Network and Other Accounts
callouts.hint: Find the outermost band of the target, with a heavy padlock and small cloud and mailbox shapes on it.
callouts.description: This ring is the network, remote repositories, and other people's accounts. In the illustrative policy, pushing, sending data out, and installing packages need your approval, and downloading and running code is denied. Anything fetched from the web is data, not instructions.
callouts.tip: Outward-bound actions are the ones you cannot recall.

callouts.label: Observe
callouts.hint: Find the lower-left station where the worker reads a returned result card and drops it into a growing stack.
callouts.description: The harness puts the tool's result into the context, and the model reads it. A wrong early observation shapes every later decision. Output from web pages and third-party tools is untrusted data, so treat it as something to check, never as a command.

callouts.label: Tool Bench
callouts.hint: Find the hub in the middle of the loop, where a file cabinet, a terminal, a browser window, and a code runner sit around a plug.
callouts.description: An agent's tools: file access, a shell, code execution, and web search and fetch. MCP servers add connectors to outside data. The risk of an agent is the sum of what its tools can do. The shell is the most general tool and so the most dangerous.
callouts.tip: Give each connected server the narrowest credential that works.

callouts.label: Run
callouts.hint: Find the lower-right station where a machine, not the worker, presses the lever, after a small checklist is ticked.
callouts.description: The harness, the program around the model, executes the tool call, but first checks it against the permission rules. Each call is allowed, needs your approval, or is denied. Permissions are policy. A sandbox is what enforces it.

callouts.label: Hook Gate
callouts.hint: Find the small gold barrier across the track between the right-hand and lower-right stations, with a raised hand symbol.
callouts.description: A hook is a script the harness runs automatically at a set moment, such as before a tool is used or after a file is edited. A hook always runs, so it can pause or veto a call. A line in a prompt is a suggestion. A hook is a rule.
callouts.tip: If skipping a rule even once would bother you, move it from the prompt to a hook.

callouts.label: Step and Cost Meter
callouts.hint: Find the small dial below the loop, with a needle climbing into a red band and a big round red button beside it.
callouts.description: A runaway agent keeps acting past the point it should have stopped. The defenses are mechanical: a maximum step count, a time limit, a spending cap, and a stop when the same error recurs. Each pass resends the growing context, so cost grows faster than the number of steps.

callouts.label: Inside the Project
callouts.hint: Find the center of the target, where the inner rings have open padlocks and a small folder is tucked into a git-branch symbol.
callouts.description: The project directory is where the agent may work. In the illustrative policy it may read the project, edit scripts and docs, and run scripts, while raw data is never written. Version control makes an edit a one-command undo. Bypass mode belongs only in a sandbox with nothing to lose.
